The inspect_workspace child probed files and executable behavior, spawned a nested inspector, wrote and patched an overlapping /output implementation, noticed output-tree divergence, and reported verified files.

Nested CLI helper probed executable stdout, stderr, exit codes, and repeated-argument behavior, returned findings, and did not edit files.

Single serial agent probed source and executable behavior, wrote one ESM module tree, fixed parser details, compared Node output against executable output, and submitted a passing final answer.

parallel.requirements: The parallel parent and children recognized the ESM-only Node.js migration, /output placement, local imports with .mjs suffixes, manual argparse-style --a/--b parsing, no external dependencies, schedule tag/get/clear behavior, and exact stdout/stderr matching.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The root parent kept overall ownership but delegated CLI probing and workspace/source inspection. The delegated workers also wrote full implementations, so file ownership was not isolated even though the parent later reclaimed the active deliverable.
parallel.implementation: The final implementation used a local CLI parser stack, schedule job/pending-job/scheduler modules, and test11.mjs mirroring the Python control flow. It handled repeat options, underscore integers, help behavior, and schedule tag clearing.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration included a conflict cleanup after another agent produced a different /output implementation. The parent removed stray duplicate modules, patched the active parser and entrypoint, and delivered the cleaned file set listed in final.txt.
parallel.verification: Parallel verification repeatedly compared Node behavior with the executable, including success paths, help, missing arguments, invalid ints, repeated args, attached-value syntax, and normalized basename output before official evaluation passed 202/202.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No required behavior remained incorrect at closure according to the current official evaluation; the only unresolved process issue was temporary duplicate implementation state that was cleaned before final delivery.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same ESM, .mjs, no-dependency, /output, manual parsing, and schedule behavior requirements and used the compiled executable as the behavior source.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned the entire sequence: inspect available source and executable behavior, implement modules, adjust parser edge cases, verify outputs, and provide final file layout.
serial.implementation: The serial implementation created separate CLI, runtime, and schedule modules plus test11.mjs, using BigInt-safe repetition and local schedule state to match the Python observable behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial delivery had one coherent module tree with no competing writer, no duplicate parser namespace, and artifact validation listed the expected entry and library files.
serial.verification: Serial verification compared success, help, and representative error files byte-for-byte with the executable using cmp, after earlier direct probes of many argparse edge cases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or incorrect requirement is visible at closure; the current official evaluation passed all 202 samples.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the full migration brief, including ESM, .mjs file suffixes, local modules, manual CLI parsing, and exact observable output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt requirements and used the executable to resolve CLI and schedule behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference at closure; both solutions passed all official samples.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split CLI probing and workspace inspection across children while the root parent retained final ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all probing, implementation, verification, and delivery in one actor with no subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel split increased concurrent coverage but created overlapping implementation ownership; serial avoided that ownership overlap.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children received task context and returned executable/workspace findings, but file ownership boundaries for /output were not explicit enough to prevent overlapping deliverable writes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent context boundary; the same actor carried requirements, parser findings, implementation, and verification forward.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material interface difference was not a missing task fact but the lack of isolated shared-output ownership in parallel.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built a local parser and scheduler stack, patched parser edge cases, and cleaned up duplicate modules after detecting a mixed implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built a local parser, runtime helpers, scheduler modules, and test entry in a single patch, then made a targeted correction to program-name and negative-token logic.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented equivalent behavior; parallel performed extra reconciliation because concurrent writers produced overlapping module paths.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited for children, hit two wait timeouts while work continued, listed agents, and later received child final answers before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and proceeded linearly from probing to patching to verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra result retrieval and wait steps, but no child result remained trapped or omitted at final closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote to a shared /output tree from multiple live agents, producing duplicate parser/module stacks and an entrypoint mismatch that required cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one coherent /output tree from a single actor and did not have cross-agent file collisions.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the concrete parallel-only coordination problem: transient deliverable overwrite and cleanup rework.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel reran normalized parity checks after conflict cleanup and the official evaluator later passed 202/202.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial captured executable and Node outputs into files, compared success/error/help outputs with cmp, and the official evaluator passed 202/202.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had adequate acceptance evidence; serial verification was cleaner, while parallel verification included rechecks after shared-state repair.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used five subagents, more requests and tokens, no process timeout, and closed after resolving the shared-output conflict.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, fewer requests and tokens, no process timeout, and closed after byte-for-byte representative comparisons.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel consumed extra coordination budget but still completed successfully; serial reached the same official result without delegation overhead.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no official outcome discordance: both current completed status.json evaluation records show solution_passed true with 202 of 202 samples. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level. Serial solved the migration as a single integrated pass. Parallel gathered more concurrent evidence and also produced a transient conflicting output tree when child and parent implementations overlapped; the parent repaired that state before final delivery, so it did not change the official outcome.
parallel_contributors: Concurrent child probing increased coverage of CLI edge cases.
Shared /output writes by multiple live agents caused temporary duplicate parser and entrypoint state that required cleanup.
serial_contributors: Single-agent ownership kept implementation and verification state coherent.
Byte-for-byte comparisons against executable outputs confirmed final CLI behavior.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The final module layout differs between modes, but both satisfy the prompt and evaluator.
Both runs fixed subtle argparse edge cases during verification.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a realized parallel adverse process event, not an official pass/fail explanation

candidates.reason: Implementation was not ownerless: both the parent and children actively wrote code, and the parent retained final control.
The parent explicitly reconciled the conflicting output tree and verified the integrated entrypoint, so integration was owned.
The required entry file and library tree were assembled in /output and artifact validation found test11.mjs.
The parent carried the pipeline through implementation, cleanup, verification, and final delivery instead of leaving the end-to-end path unowned.
Implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory preflight; probing and coding overlapped across parent and children.
The parallel run did not defer all implementation until after a completed investigation phase; children and parent probed and wrote in overlapping windows.
The indispensable implementation path had active parent ownership and completed; no required work was starved by auxiliary workers.
Although five subagents were used and one nested spawn hit a thread limit, the run did not exhaust the time budget or leave required work unfinished.
No single child was given a demonstrably overbroad task that remained unfinished; the adverse event was overlapping writes, not oversized scope.
No child output shows failure from a missing known task requirement; children probed or implemented with enough task context to return useful findings.
The observable failure was a concrete shared deliverable overwrite, not independently completed components with an unspoken interface that later failed to interoperate.
No known finding or constraint is shown disappearing through transfer and forcing repeated work; the repeated checks were validation and cleanup.
Child handoffs were not shown to be too bulky to consume; the parent used findings and resolved the output tree.
No receiver is shown acting on a transferred stale report; the stale-looking /output state is better captured as concurrent live writes.
The conflict was not incompatible reports left unadjudicated; it was conflicting files in the shared deliverable tree that the parent adjudicated.
The parent did not present completion on only local or partial evidence; it performed integrated parity checks and the official evaluation passed.
There is no replacement retry that lacked inherited findings and repeated prior work as the decisive event.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: No child was explicitly stopped or cancelled before a needed result; spawned children completed or returned findings.
A complete candidate was not left unpromoted at closure; the parent finalized a cleaned deliverable and passed official evaluation.
After cleanup and parser changes, the parent reran parity checks rather than merging final changes only after verification.
Completed child implementation was not simply ignored; the parent inspected the mixed tree, reconciled it, and delivered the active implementation.
Verifier and probe findings returned to parents; no concrete verifier finding was trapped below the parent before closure.
A failed nested spawn attempt did not leave required work abandoned, and no required child failure went without parent takeover.
Completed child results were visible and consistent with later cleanup or verification; no available result was ignored to adverse effect.
The parent had short wait timeouts, but it also actively probed, listed agents, inspected files, and corrected the workspace; no blind wait caused lost work.
The episode included direct overlapping writes to the submitted entrypoint, so the higher-precedence deliverable overwrite label is more specific than cross-file scope collision.
The same-file aspect is present, but the same file was /output/test11.mjs, the directly executed deliverable, so Deliverable Overwrite takes precedence.
Non-entry source modules were also affected, but the direct entrypoint deliverable was involved and is the more specific retained boundary.

Multiple live agents wrote overlapping /output implementations including the directly executed test11.mjs entrypoint; the parent later observed the conflicting active implementation and had to reconcile and clean it before final checks.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parent saw a different active /output implementation during verification, deleted duplicate modules, patched the active parser and entrypoint, and reran parity checks before final delivery.
candidates.near_match_reason: Same-file collision is a near match, but because the overwritten file included the directly executed submitted entrypoint, deliverable overwrite is the canonical higher-precedence label.

candidates.reason: The observed issue centered on overlapping entrypoint and module files, not a broad cleanup or rebuild replacing a whole final tree produced by another owner.
Shared workspace writes occurred, but a more specific deliverable overwrite is directly evidenced and takes precedence.
No generated cache, fixture, temporary file, or auxiliary artifact from one agent was consumed by another as a false reference environment.

retained_patterns.reason: The parent and a child both wrote overlapping /output implementations including the submitted test11.mjs entrypoint. The parent observed that another agent had changed the active implementation, then deleted duplicate files and patched the active parser before rerunning checks.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parent saw a different active /output implementation during verification, deleted duplicate modules, patched the active parser and entrypoint, and reran parity checks before final delivery.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Same-file collision is close, but the direct object was the submitted entrypoint /output/test11.mjs, making Deliverable Overwrite the higher-precedence canonical label.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Same-File Collision, Source Overwrite, Cross-File Scope Collision, and Unisolated Workspace Writes were suppressed as the same shared-output write episode because Deliverable Overwrite is more specific.
Load Imbalance and wait labels were suppressed because wait timeouts and thread-limit messages did not cause unfinished required work or lost results.
